title: Presto, presto, pria ch'ei venga
subtitle: Masetto, Zerlina, Don Giovanni, Leporello, Donna Elvira, Donna Anna, Don Ottavio and the servants' chorus: the opening of the finale from Don Giovanni, Act 1 (No. 13)

passages.label: Allegro assai: Presto, presto, pria ch'ei venga · Senti, senti! dove vai? · Che capriccio ha nella testa?
Capirò se m'è fedele · Quell' ingrato, quel crudele (sotto voce)
Sù! svegliatevi da bravi · Alla stanza della danza (Don Giovanni)
Sù, svegliatevi da bravi (the servants' chorus)
Andante: Tra quest' arbori celata · Zerlinetta, mia garbata · fortunata io ti vo' far
Masetto? · La bella tua Zerlina non può più star senza di te
Allegretto: Adesso fate core · Sì, sì, facciamo core · andiamo tutti tre
Bisogna aver coraggio · L'amica dice bene · Il passo è periglioso
Menuetto: Signor, guardate un poco · Al volto ed alla voce · Zi! zi! · Grazie di tanto onore (to the bar before the Adagio)

licences.source: W. A. Mozart, Don Giovanni, K. 527 (1787), Act 1 scenes 17–20, No. 13 Finale, from its beginning to the bar before the Adagio ("Protegga il giusto cielo")

licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score, which differ from the libretto in places: pormi vo' (libretto por mi vo'); quell' ingrato; Ah! sei vede (libretto s'ei vede); sò; Sù!; ed a tutti a abbondanza (libretto in abbondanza); gran rifreschi (libretto rinfreschi); non scoppar (libretto scappar); gioja; E chiuso là; dì; andiamo tutti tre (libretto tutti e tre); Zi! zi!; Io temo pel caro sposo. Leporello's last word, d'amor, is split by the end of the piece: d'a- here, -mor! on the first bar of the Adagio.

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 112–124, bars 1–250 of No. 13 (to page 124, system 3, bar 1, the bar before the Adagio)
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages in three chunks (pp. 112–115, 116–119, 120–124): the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by fresh checkers, whose findings were corrected. Don Ottavio's part and the servants' chorus (printed on one treble-clef staff, tenors and basses on shared stems) are written at sounding pitch; the chorus is written out as two parts, heard in the mix, with no role. Kept as printed: in bar 150 the fourth note of Zerlina and of the piano is D sharp by the bar rule (the sharp is printed on the second D only; possibly D natural intended). The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. Allegro assai 4/4 C major bars 1–91, Andante 3/4 F major bars 92–138, Allegretto 2/4 bars 139–217, Menuetto 3/4 bars 218–250. Playback tempo from five complete recordings (Giulini 1959, Klemperer 1966, Barenboim 1975, Haitink 1984, I. Fischer 2026), median track times: bars 1–91 1:59 (Allegro assai ♩ = 184); bars 92–168 2:28 and bars 169–250 2:16, divided between the sections by the Menuetto's share of the second span in the two sets that give it its own track (Fischer 1:09 of 2:13, Currentzis 1:02 of 1:57): Andante ♩ = 78, Allegretto ♩ = 91, Menuetto ♩ = 83; about 6¾ minutes in all. Mozart gives the words only.
